Daughters: Ireland in Conflict 1798 (2003); SC viii 897–915.
 Contemporary reviews of 1820 are on the whole positive about the miscellaneous poems
in the volume, including SP — Blackwood’s vii (September 1820) singling out its ‘affecting’
qualities, though the comprehensively disapproving notice of the volume in the Quarterly
Review xxvi (1821) taxes SP with metaphorical incoherence masked by ‘the tricks of a mere
poetical harlequin’. Regularly quoted in magazines and annuals, SP was one of a small
number of poems that helped to create S.’s reputation as a lyricist in the early nineteenth
century (White ii 415).
 Text from 1820. Significant variants only from the draft in Nbks 11 and 12 and the fair
copy in Harvard Nbk 1 are recorded in the notes. The capitalisation of Harvard Nbk 1 has
been preferred.
 Published in 1820, MYRS v 47–61, MYRS vi 238–9 (facsimile and transcription of
